claim: There exists a polynomial-time reduction from the EXP-complete problem LSBS to the NP-complete problem LFPF, using input padding to convert an exponential-time reduction into a polynomial-time one.
falsifier: One can implement the reduction as described and verify that it runs in polynomial time relative to the padded input, and that it correctly maps LSBS instances to LFPF instances.

conditions: the exponential-time reduction from LSBS to LFPF exists (Theorem 3.8)
the input is sufficiently padded to make the reduction polynomial in the padded length
exclusions: limited to the specific problems LSBS and LFPF as defined in the source; the reduction is non-standard because it does not preserve complexity relative to the original input size

title: The reduction from LSBS–polynomial-time reduction theorem
